content.title: About
content.content: Meat lasagna is a classic Italian dish made of layers of pasta sheets, meat sauce (usually ground beef), tomato sauce, cheese and sometimes béchamel. It is baked until the top turns golden, resulting in a flavorful and hearty dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first written mention of lasagna dates back to the 13th century, but the modern meat‑based version became popular in the United States in the early 20th century.
The word “lasagna” comes from the Latin “lasanum,” meaning “cooking pot.”
In the United States, July 29 is celebrated as National Lasagna Day.
Traditional Italian lasagna often uses a ragù (meat ragout) rather than plain ground beef.
There are more than 30 recognized variations of lasagna, including vegetarian, seafood and even dessert versions.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat in the dish provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Hard cheeses add calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant linked to heart health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of carbs, fats and protein makes lasagna a substantial source of energy for active individuals.

items.title: High calorie and fat content
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable for those monitoring weight.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should choose lactose‑free or dairy‑free cheese alternatives.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked ground meat may harbor pathogens; ensure the meat reaches an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lasagna is typically cut into serving portions and served hot, sprinkled with fresh basil or grated Parmesan. It pairs well with a light salad, garlic bread, and a glass of red wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, portion and freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 2 months. Reheat until the interior reaches 74 °C (165 °F).
